This regulation may be cited as the Motor Vehicles Securities Regulation 1995 . ˙ Commencement 2. This regulation commences on 17 April 1995. ˙ Definitions 3. In this regulation— “approved form” means the form approved by the chief executive under section 7. 1 “mine” has the same meaning as in the Mineral Resources Act 1989 . “motor vehicle” see section 4. “VIN” means a unique vehicle identification number on a vehicle’s compliance plate that is the same as the identification number marked on the chassis or another part of the vehicle. ˙ Meaning of “motor vehicle”—Act, s 5(1) 4.(1) “Motor vehicle” means— (a) a land vehicle propelled by anything other than humans, animals, gravity or the wind; or (b) a vehicle (other than farm machinery), for example a trailer, 1 Section 7 (Using approved form is prescribed way of applying for all types of registration—Act, ss 7(1)(a), 8(2)(a) and 14(1)(a)) s5 4 s6 Motor Vehicles Securities Regulation 1995 designed to be attached to a vehicle described in paragraph (a). (2) However, a “motor vehicle” does not include— (a) a train or hovercraft; or (b) a vehicle used, or intended to be used, primarily in mining. ˙ Fees 5. The schedule sets out the fees payable under the Act. 2 ˙ Prescribed particulars to be entered in register 6. Under section 6(2)(f) 3 of the Act the particulars are as follows— (a) the time (by New South Wales reckoning) the application to register the security interest is lodged; (b) the date (by New South Wales reckoning) of registration of a full, or partial, discharge of an interest; (c) the reference number for the interest supplied by the holder of the interest; (d) if the type of instrument involved in the security interest is a hire purchase agreement, lease or mortgage—the type of instrument; (e) if another type of instrument is involved—that the type of instrument is other than a hire purchase agreement, lease or mortgage; (f) for each vehicle to which the interest applies, the vehicle’s— (i) body type; and (ii) make; and (iii) year of manufacture; and (iv) engine number; and 2 There is no fee for applying for registration of a full, or partial, discharge of a security interest. 3 Section 6 (Register) of the Act s 7 5 s 10 Motor Vehicles Securities Regulation 1995 (v) chassis number or VIN; and (vi) registration number under the Transport Infrastructure (Roads) Act 1991 or a law, of another State, for registration of motor vehicles; and (vii) State of registration under subparagraph (vi); (g) the day the registration of the security interest expires. ˙ Using approved form is prescribed way of applying for all types of registration—Act, ss 7(1)(a), 8(2)(a) and 14(1)(a) 7.(1) The chief executive may approve forms for use under the Act. (2) An application under the Act for any type of registration must be in the approved form. ˙ Prescribed change in particulars entered in register 8.(1) Under section 18 4 a prescribed change is any change. (2) An application to change particulars entered in the register must be in the approved form. ˙ Application to correct an error 9.(1) A person may apply to the chief executive for correction of an error, omission or failure mentioned in section 19 5 of the Act. (2) A person must apply in writing. (3) The chief executive may waive the fee for an application under subsection (1), if the chief executive considers it appropriate. ˙ Statement of current and past information compiled from the register 10.(1) The chief executive may issue a statement of information about a security interest compiled from— 4 Section 18 (Rectification of register) of the Act 5 Section 19 (Correction of errors) of the Act s 11 6 s 12 Motor Vehicles Securities Regulation 1995 (a) the register after 16 April 1995; or (b) information relating to the register after that date. (2) No compensation is payable by the State, the chief executive or a person acting under the chief executive’s direction for any loss caused by, or partly by, relying on a statement under this section. (3) A statement of information must contain a disclaimer setting out the effect of subsection (2). ˙ Inspection of applications, list of interests and limits on access to them 11. The chief executive may— (a) supply a list of the registered security interests held by a person to the person, but not to anyone else; and (b) allow a person to inspect any application under the Act, other than an application for approval as an account holder. ˙ Approval to hold an account for fees payable under the Act 12.(1) The chief executive may give approval for a person to hold an account for fees payable by the person under the Act. (2) An application for approval must be in the approved form. (3) The chief executive must inform the person, in writing, as follows— (a) whether approval is given or refused; (b) if approval is given—any terms of the approval; (c) if approval is refused—the reasons for refusal. (4) Terms of an approval are to be decided by the chief executive. (5) While the approval is in force, the account holder must pay the fees within 14 days of the chief executive posting, or sending by fax or other electronic means, notice of the fees to the address or number last given, in writing, to the chief executive by the holder for the purpose of the account. (6) If the chief executive considers an account holder has not complied s 13 7 s 14 Motor Vehicles Securities Regulation 1995 with subsection (5) or a term of the approval, the chief executive may cancel or suspend the approval. ˙ Computer software packages to access on-line information 13.(1) A person may apply to purchase computer software packages to access information available on-line under this regulation. (2) An application to purchase a software package must be in the approved form. ˙ Recognised States—Act, s 38(1) 14.
